Exercise: Reverse Triceps Bench Press

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- triple_extension

Primary Muscles:

- triceps

Secondary Muscles:

- chest
- shoulders

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
ATP-PC and glycolytic

Recovery Time:
24 hours

Goals:

- strength_building
- tricep_hypertrophy

Contraindications:
None

Exercise Variations:

- name: Reverse Triceps Pushdown, equipment: cable machine

Substitution Options:

- name: Triceps Dips, equipment: bench
- name: Close-Grip Bench Press, equipment: barbell

Instructions:

- Lie back on a flat bench. Using a close, supinated grip (around shoulder width), lift the bar from the rack and hold it straight over you with your arms locked extended in front of you and perpendicular to the floor. This will be your starting position.
- As you breathe in, come down slowly until you feel the bar on your middle chest. Tip: Make sure that as opposed to a regular bench press, you keep the elbows close to the torso at all times in order to maximize triceps involvement.
- After a second pause, bring the bar back to the starting position as you breathe out and push the bar using your triceps muscles. Lock your arms in the contracted position, hold for a second and then start coming down slowly again. Tip: It should take at least twice as long to go down than to come up.
- Repeat the movement for the prescribed amount of repetitions.
- When you are done, place the bar back in the rack.
